The last trace of his existence is in 1144 when he took over the head of rgyal lha khang.").

person.persName: zul phul bya 'dul ba 'dzin pa chen po
person.note: Born in 1091 at gTsang rong gyung and died at the age of 76 in Zul phu according to [R894SIKE]: 109. [W4T5ZMUP]: 38 accordingly proposes the dates 1091-1166. [VKBZTBWN], fol. 3b6 reports that he was born the year rNgog lo (ID:3786) came back to Tibet, i.e., ca. 1092. On his life, based on the Zul phu mkhan byang chub rin chen dpal bzang po'i rnam par thar pa (ID:6715), see [W4T5ZMUP]: 40. It is unclear whether he is the same person as rGya 'dul ba 'dzin pa (ID:4193). The [NA9AMDH6] distinguishes two "rGya 'dul 'dzin" - the elder (ID: 3941) and the younger (ID:4193) - and a "Bya 'dul 'dzin brTson 'grus 'bar" (student of 'Bre chen po). In contrast, the [R894SIKE] only mentions one "rGya 'dul 'dzin" (the elder), distinct from "Bya 'dul 'dzin" (who was ordained by 'Bre). [VKBZTBWN], fol. 6b5-6 and [8VLVHDR2], fol. 14b5 report that he was ordained by 'Bre and received from him the name in religion brTson 'grus 'bar. A number of the same teachers are mentioned for rGya 'dul 'dzin the younger and Bya 'dul 'dzin but, for instance, the latter's studies with rGya 'dul 'dzin the older took place when he was a retired abbot, whereas the former's studies with him took place when he was still abbot. Further, rGya 'dul 'dzin the younger became abbot of dGa' ba sdong and Bya 'dul abbot of Zul phu. This suggests they might have been distinct persons.

Listed in the group of Phya pa (ID:3831)'s students called the "four noble ones" (jo sras mi bzhi), comprising rNgog ra mo (ID:3847), bSod nams rtse mo (ID:3838), Khu Ne tso (ID:3849), and gNyos dPal le (ID:3850). Biographical sketch in [FDEWZ2NZ]: 289-291. [FDEWZ2NZ]: 264 adopts the dates 1134-1170 (from the lHo rong chos 'byung) rather than the dates 1146-1182 (from the Deb ther sngon po), which [HM43XTRK] adopts. He studied all the tantric cycles of the rNgog, and was proficient as well in Perfection of wisdom, epistemology, debate, etc.

First Karmapa. His birth name was dGe 'phel ([Y6NGTTC6]: 24). His alternative names and epithets are listed in [Y6NGTTC6]: 5 and 27, which also lists the main information on his life found in early sources. Dus gsum mkhyen pa (ID:3855), Sho sgom (ID:3857), and Phag mo gru pa (ID:3856) are known as the "grub thob mi gsum" and as the "khams pa mi gsum." According to Dus gsum mkhyen pa'i rnam thar in Si tu Chos kyi 'byung gnas's Karma kam tshang gser 'phreng (cited in [I58Z22ET]: 408, n. 42), Dus gsum mkhyen became known as one of the "khams pa mi gsum" during his stays in gSang phu (ID:4332) (gsang phur yang bzhugs te | khams pa mi gsum du grags |).

[EZ5JXHJY]: 356 and n. 16 takes him to be the same person as Tshul khrims snying po (ID:6157) and gives the dates 1116-1169. It is assumed here to be the same person as "gsal ston sho sgom," student of sGam po pa (ID:4189).

person.note: Fl. late 12th to early 13th c. [MPRU5QUC] records the name of this abbot as "'Jam dpal seng ge." He received the name "'jam pa'i rdo rje" during a tantric initiation ([5632TFMN]: 312 and n. 11). [AT6DUUJJ]: 23 discusses his dates, suggesting he lived towards the end of the 12th century.. [5632TFMN]: 313 suggests he may have passed away in ca. 1227.

person.persName: chos grags gnyis pa gzhon nu rin chen

person.note: Fl. late 13th to early 14th c. We assume that the gZhon nu rin chen who was abbot of gSang phu is the same person as the author of the two works by gZhon nu rin chen. The latter is characterized in [8H6M69W4], No. 15506, as the "student of Nyang" (nyang gi slob ma), which, in view of the colophon of (ID:4625), is Nyang bran pa Chos kyi ye shes (ID:3876) rather than Nyang bran pa Chos kyi seng ge (ID:3844).

Scholar from Sadnagara in Bengal, active in Tibet in the 1430s and 1440s, on the invitation of the Phag mo gru. See [MKF6XDW8]: 69-70, n. 120, [Q922IUFM]: 13.
